observation_summary: A call to TimeSeries.createCopy(startIndex, endIndex) is made when startIndex and endIndex (computed from time periods) can be in the wrong order, producing an IllegalArgumentException "Requires start <= end." The outer createCopy(period, period) path computes integer indexes and only checks for endIndex < 0 but does not check for startIndex > endIndex, so an exception is thrown instead of returning an empty series.
reasoning_summary: The failure is caused by a missing validation/guard: after mapping requested time periods to integer indexes the code fails to check the ordering (startIndex <= endIndex) before calling the index-based createCopy. The immediate fix is to add the missing check (or otherwise handle the empty-range case) in the period-based createCopy path. This is a predicate/validation error (Checking) rather than a pure assignment or a larger design change.
